components.note: 王 (jade, written without its dot) — 玩 originally meant to handle and admire a piece of jade, extending to 'to play, to have fun.'
元 (yuán) gives a sound distantly related to wán, having drifted apart over time.
王 (jade, written without its dot) — 玩 originally meant to handle and admire a piece of jade, extending to 'to play, to have fun.'
元 (yuán) gives a sound distantly related to wán, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他只是拿新手机玩玩,没打算认真研究。
example.pinyin: tā zhǐshì ná xīn shǒujī wánwán, méi dǎsuàn rènzhēn yánjiū.
example.english: He's just playing around with the new phone, not planning to seriously study it.
example.fact: The IBM Simon, released in 1994, is widely considered the first smartphone — it had a touchscreen, email, and even a calendar nearly 15 years before the iPhone. It weighed over half a kilogram and its battery lasted less than an hour of talk time.

components.note: 爪 and 彐 (two hands, reaching from opposite sides) — a simplified form of 爭, grabbing for the same thing.
亅 (the object) — what the two hands are struggling over, giving 争 its meaning 'to contend, compete, fight for.'
Rain — an older semantic root kept from the character's older form.

example.hanzi: 两家科技巨头正在人工智能领域争霸。
example.pinyin: liǎng jiā kējì jùtóu zhèngzài réngōng zhìnéng lǐngyù zhēngbà.
example.english: The two tech giants are contending for dominance in the field of artificial intelligence.
example.fact: Invasive Argentine ant colonies along the Mediterranean coast have merged across huge stretches of territory into a single 'supercolony' spanning thousands of kilometers, eliminating rival colonies in their struggle for dominance. Scientists consider it one of the largest cooperative units ever documented in the animal kingdom.

components.note: 人 (person) appears in 侵's structure, reflecting the character's original picture of a person creeping forward to raid or encroach on another's territory.
帚 (broom) sits alongside the person element; early forms show someone advancing with a broom-like tool, an image of stealthy invasion that later broadened to any act of encroachment.
犭 (dog) — 犯 originally related to a dog attacking, later extended to any act of violation
㔾 (jié) gives a sound distantly related to 犯's reading fàn, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 未经许可复制别人的作品属于侵犯版权。
example.pinyin: wèijīng xǔkě fùzhì biérén de zuòpǐn shǔyú qīnfàn bǎnquán.
example.english: Copying someone else's work without permission constitutes copyright infringement.
example.fact: The Berne Convention of 1886 was the first international agreement to protect authors' rights across borders, and it still underpins copyright law in more than 180 countries today. It introduced the principle that copyright exists automatically the moment a work is created, without needing registration.

components.note: A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.
一 (one) — relates to 百's meaning 'hundred,' a large round number built from 'one.'
白 (bái) gives a sound hint — 百 is pronounced bǎi, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

The traditional form 萬 was a pictograph of a scorpion, its raised tail and legs later abstracted into the compact 万 shape. The link between 'scorpion' and 'ten thousand' is a sound borrowing rather than a meaning connection, one of many such loans in Chinese writing.

example.hanzi: 这座桥的建造花费了超过一百万美元。
example.pinyin: zhè zuò qiáo de jiànzào huāfèi le chāoguò yībǎiwàn měiyuán.
example.english: Building this bridge cost more than one million dollars.
example.fact: The Golden Gate Bridge, completed in 1937, cost about $35 million to build — equivalent to well over a billion dollars today — and its total length of cable wire, if unwound, would circle the earth more than three times.

components.note: 无 simplifies 無, whose early form pictured a dancer waving decorated sleeves. That dance image was borrowed for its sound to write the abstract idea of 'nothing, without,' completely displacing the original meaning of dancing.
心 (heart/mind) — 意 relates to thought, intention, and meaning, things of the mind.
音 (yīn) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading has drifted from yì, though both share a similar vowel.

example.hanzi: 我无意打扰你,只是想确认一下时间。
example.pinyin: wǒ wúyì dǎrǎo nǐ, zhǐshì xiǎng quèrèn yīxià shíjiān.
example.english: I didn't mean to disturb you; I just wanted to confirm the time.
example.fact: Penicillin, one of the most important medical discoveries in history, was found completely by accident in 1928 when Alexander Fleming noticed mold had killed bacteria in a petri dish he'd left uncovered. He almost discarded the dish before noticing the unusual clearing around the mold.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 温 originally described warm water.
昷 (wēn) gives the sound — an exact match with 温.
Sun — warmth comes from the sun.
Gives the sound yuán, related to nuǎn but drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 壁炉让整个房间变得温暖起来。
example.pinyin: bìlú ràng zhěnggè fángjiān biàn de wēnnuǎn qǐlái.
example.english: The fireplace made the whole room warm.
example.fact: The Gulf Stream carries roughly 30 times more water than all the world's rivers combined, moving warm water from the Gulf of Mexico up toward Northern Europe. It's a major reason London stays milder in winter than cities at similar latitudes in Canada.

components.note: 王 (jade, written as the radical for 玉) — 珠 names a round gem or bead.
朱 (zhū) is an exact match for the sound of 珠.
宀 (a roof) — a house where valuables are kept
玉 (jade) — the treasure kept safe inside

example.hanzi: 她把祖母留下的珠宝锁进了保险箱。
example.pinyin: tā bǎ zǔmǔ liú xià de zhūbǎo suǒ jìn le bǎoxiǎnxiāng.
example.english: She locked the jewelry her grandmother left behind into the safe.
example.fact: The Hope Diamond, one of the most famous jewels in the world, is believed to have originated from the Kollur Mine in India and is now valued at over $250 million. Its deep blue color comes from trace amounts of boron atoms in its crystal structure.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 提 relates to lifting or carrying something by hand.
是 (shì) gives a hint of the sound — 提 is pronounced tí, a connection that has shifted over time.
走 (to walk/run) — 起 relates to standing up and setting into motion.
己 (jǐ) gives a close sound cue — 起 is pronounced qǐ, sharing the same final sound.

example.hanzi: 每次提起那次旅行,他都会笑出来。
example.pinyin: měi cì tíqǐ nà cì lǚxíng, tā dōu huì xiào chūlái.
example.english: Every time that trip comes up, he laughs.
example.fact: Smell-triggered memories are so vivid they have their own name, the 'Proust phenomenon,' because the brain's olfactory bulb connects almost directly to the memory and emotion centers. Studies have found that scent-cued memories feel more emotionally intense than the same memories cued by words or pictures.

meanings: variant of 大夥|大伙[da4 huo3]

components.note: A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
亻 (person) — 伙 relates to people who share meals or work together.
火 (huǒ) gives the sound — an exact match with 伙's reading huǒ.

example.hanzi: 周末大伙一起去海边野餐吧。
example.pinyin: zhōumò dàhuǒ yīqǐ qù hǎibiān yěcān ba.
example.english: Let's all go to the beach for a picnic together this weekend.
example.fact: Emperor penguins survive Antarctic winters by huddling together in groups of thousands, constantly rotating positions so no single bird stays on the frigid outer edge too long. This collective strategy can raise the temperature at the center of the huddle to nearly 37°C even when it's -40°C outside.

components.note: 口 (a vessel), shown four times — a set of cooking vessels.
犬 (a dog) — guarding the vessels, the source of 器's meaning 'vessel, tool, instrument.'
宀 (roof, building) sits atop 官, evoking a hall or office.

㠯 depicts a mound or garrison beneath the roof; together the two pieces pictured a government building where officials presided, a meaning later extended to bodily 'organs' as functional units within the body.

example.hanzi: 心脏是人体最重要的器官之一。
example.pinyin: xīnzàng shì rén tǐ zuì zhòngyào de qìguān zhī yī.
example.english: The heart is one of the most important organs in the human body.
example.fact: The human liver is the only internal organ that can regrow to nearly its full size after part of it is removed — even after losing up to 70%, it can regenerate within a few months. This regenerative ability is what makes living-donor liver transplants possible.

components.note: 屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'
片 (a slice/plate) — 版 originally referred to a wooden printing block
反 (fǎn) gives the sound — an exact match with 版's reading bǎn

example.hanzi: 这本小说去年正式出版。
example.pinyin: zhè běn xiǎoshuō qùnián zhèngshì chūbǎn.
example.english: This novel was officially published last year.
example.fact: Johannes Gutenberg's movable-type printing press, introduced around 1440, sparked a mass-publishing revolution in Europe — within 50 years, over 20 million books had been printed, more than all European scribes had produced by hand in the previous thousand years combined.

components.note: 刀 (knife) — relates directly to 切's meaning 'to cut.'
七 (qī) gives a sound hint — 切 is pronounced qiè, sharing the same initial consonant.
斤 (an axe) — cutting through something.
米 (grain, in the simplified form; a bundle of thread in the traditional 斷) — the material being cut, giving 断 its meaning 'to break off, cut, sever.'

example.hanzi: 暴风雪切断了整个村庄的电力供应。
example.pinyin: bàofēngxuě qiēduàn le zhěnggè cūnzhuāng de diànlì gōngyìng.
example.english: The blizzard cut off the entire village's power supply.
example.fact: In 2003, a single software bug in an Ohio power plant's alarm system helped trigger the Northeast Blackout, cutting off electricity to 55 million people across the US and Canada for up to two days. It remains one of the largest blackouts in history.

components.note: 王 (jade, written as 王 in components) — 玫 originally described a type of fine jade or gem.
攵 gives a sound only distantly related to méi today, having drifted apart over time.
王 (jade) — 瑰 originally described a fine, precious stone.
鬼 (guǐ) gives a sound close to guī, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 他送了她一束红玫瑰。
example.pinyin: tā sòng le tā yī shù hóng méiguī.
example.english: He gave her a bouquet of red roses.
example.fact: Roses are among the oldest cultivated flowers on Earth — fossil evidence suggests wild roses existed 35 million years ago, and archaeologists have found rose motifs in Egyptian tombs, pointing to cultivation stretching back thousands of years.

components.note: 山 (mountain) — 崇 describes something towering high, like a mountain, extending to 'to revere.'
宗 (zōng) shares the rhyme -ong with chóng, though the initial has drifted from z- to ch- over time.
手 (hand), shown twice, side by side — two hands pressed together in a gesture of respect, giving 拜 its meaning 'to bow, to pay respects.'

example.hanzi: 很多孩子从小就崇拜自己的父亲。
example.pinyin: hěn duō háizi cóngxiǎo jiù chóngbài zìjǐ de fùqīn.
example.english: Many children have worshipped their fathers since they were young.
example.fact: Ancient Egyptians worshipped the sun god Ra as one of their most powerful deities, believing he sailed across the sky each day in a solar barge and battled the serpent Apep every night to be reborn at dawn. Sun worship even influenced the alignment of monuments like the pyramids.

components.note: 止 (foot) at the top of 前 shows movement.
舟 (boat) beneath the foot completes the original picture of a foot stepping into a boat to move ahead, which is how 前 came to mean 'front' or 'before.'
女 (woman) sits at the base of the character.
彐-shaped strokes above picture a hand holding a broom, an old image of a wife managing the household.

example.hanzi: 他和前妻仍然保持着朋友关系。
example.pinyin: tā hé qiánqī réngrán bǎochí zhe péngyǒu guānxì.
example.english: He and his ex-wife still remain friends.
example.fact: Ancient Rome allowed unilateral no-fault divorce as early as the 2nd century BC, making it one of the earliest legal systems to let either spouse end a marriage without proving wrongdoing — a right many modern legal systems didn't grant until the 20th century.

components.note: 丿 (something falling) — an object slipping away.
夫 (a hand/person) — the object slipping out of a hand, giving 失 its meaning 'to lose.'
攵 (a striking hand) — 败 relates to being struck down or defeated.
贝 (bèi) gives a sound close to bài, sharing the same initial.

者's ancient form pictured leaves or stalks growing from a plant, an image later borrowed purely for its sound to mark 'the one who' or 'the thing that,' as in 读者 (reader) — the plant meaning has been completely lost.

example.hanzi: 没有人愿意被称为失败者。
example.pinyin: méiyǒu rén yuànyì bèi chēng wéi shībàizhě.
example.english: No one wants to be called a loser.
example.fact: Wilbur and Orville Wright endured years of crashes and failed glider tests at Kitty Hawk before their December 1903 flight lasted just 12 seconds — yet it became the first sustained, controlled, powered flight in human history.

components.note: 耂 (a variant of 老, 'old') — 考 relates to careful examination and testing
丂 gives a loose sound connection to 考's reading kǎo
马 (horse) — 验 originally related to examining or testing horses, later extended to 'to test, examine, verify'
佥 (qiān) gives a loose sound connection to 验's reading yàn

example.hanzi: 这场比赛是对他体力的一次考验。
example.pinyin: zhè chǎng bǐsài shì duì tā tǐlì de yī cì kǎoyàn.
example.english: This competition is a test of his physical strength.
example.fact: NASA astronaut candidates undergo a water-survival test where they're strapped into a mock capsule and dropped into a pool, then must escape while inverted and disoriented — an ordeal deliberately designed to simulate emergency splashdown conditions.

components.note: 罒 (a net) — the law closing in around wrongdoing
非 (wrong) — the wrongdoing itself, caught in the net
彳 depicts a step with the left foot; together with 亍 (a step with the right foot), 行 shows a person walking or moving.
亍 depicts a step with the right foot, complementing 彳 to form the idea of walking or travel.

example.hanzi: 法庭正在审理他的罪行。
example.pinyin: fǎtíng zhèngzài shěnlǐ tā de zuìxíng.
example.english: The court is currently trying his offense.
example.fact: The Nuremberg trials of 1945-46 were the first international tribunals to prosecute leaders for war crimes and crimes against humanity, establishing legal precedents — like rejecting 'just following orders' as a defense — that still shape international criminal law today.

components.note: 攵 (an action/to strike) — 效 relates to the result produced by an action
交 (jiāo) gives a sound close to 效's reading xiào
艹 (grass) — a bundle of grass or straw carried as a load
力 (strength) — the effort of lifting and carrying the heavy load

example.hanzi: 他愿意为公司效劳多年。
example.pinyin: tā yuànyì wèi gōngsī xiàoláo duō nián.
example.english: He is willing to serve the company for many years.
example.fact: Honeybee workers spend their roughly six-week lifespan working themselves to death for the colony — foraging bees fly up to 800 kilometers over their lifetime and can visit over 2,000 flowers in a single day of gathering for the hive.

components.note: 日 (sun/day) — relates to 时's meaning of 'time, season'; the phonetic part of the character was later replaced by 寸 in the simplified form
衣 (clothing) — 装 relates to clothes, dress, and attire
壮 (zhuàng) gives the sound — 装 is pronounced zhuāng, a close match

example.hanzi: 巴黎每年都会举办著名的时装秀。
example.pinyin: bālí měi nián dōu huì jǔbàn zhùmíng de shízhuāng xiù.
example.english: Paris holds a famous fashion show every year.
example.fact: Paris Fashion Week traces its roots to the Chambre Syndicale de la Couture Parisienne, founded in 1868, making it one of the oldest continuously running fashion institutions in the world — over 150 years before today's livestreamed runway shows.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — 稍 relates to a small amount of grain.
肖 (to resemble) — grain 禾 that only resembles a full harvest, a slightly smaller amount, gave 稍 its meaning 'slightly, a little.'

后 was originally a separate character picturing a ruler with an open mouth issuing commands, the source of meanings like 'queen' or 'empress.' Simplified Chinese reused this shape to also stand for 後 ('behind, after'), so the modern 后 quietly carries two unrelated histories in one form.

example.hanzi: 会议稍后开始,请大家先坐好。
example.pinyin: huìyì shāohòu kāishǐ, qǐng dàjiā xiān zuò hǎo.
example.english: The meeting will start shortly; everyone please take a seat first.
example.fact: Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth, so whenever you look at the Sun, you're actually seeing it as it appeared slightly earlier — if it suddenly vanished, we wouldn't know for over eight minutes.

components.note: Hand — moving things is done by hand.
Gives the sound bān, matching the character's reading.
宀 (roof) — 家 is about a home, the space under a roof.
豕 (shǐ, 'pig') supplies the ancient sound for 家; keeping a pig under one's roof was also a practical sign of a household in ancient China, though the modern readings jiā and shǐ no longer rhyme.

example.hanzi: 我们下个月要搬家到另一个城市。
example.pinyin: wǒmen xià gè yuè yào bānjiā dào lìng yī gè chéngshì.
example.english: We're moving to another city next month.
example.fact: According to US Census data, the average American moves about 11.7 times in their lifetime, a notably higher rate of internal migration than in most other developed nations, largely driven by job mobility.

meanings: to host (a TV or radio program etc)

components.note: 丶 (a dot) — represents the burning flame atop a lamp.
王 here depicts the base and stand of an oil lamp, not its usual meaning 'king' — the one who tends the flame became linked to 'master, lord, main.'
扌 (hand) — relates directly to 持's meaning 'to hold, maintain.'
寺 (sì) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from chí.

example.hanzi: 她将主持今晚的颁奖典礼。
example.pinyin: tā jiāng zhǔchí jīnwǎn de bānjiǎng diǎnlǐ.
example.english: She will host tonight's award ceremony.
example.fact: The Academy Awards ceremony has aired live on television since 1953, and its unscripted hosting segments are considered so unpredictable that producers build in extensive contingency plans, including backup hosts kept on standby in case of an emergency.

components.note: 田 (field) — represents farmland.
力 (strength/effort) — someone strong enough to work the fields gave 男 its meaning 'male, man.'
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 一名男子在公园里跑步锻炼。
example.pinyin: yī míng nánzǐ zài gōngyuán lǐ pǎobù duànliàn.
example.english: A man was running and exercising in the park.
example.fact: The men's 100-meter world record, held by Usain Bolt at 9.58 seconds since 2009, requires reaching speeds of over 44 km/h at peak stride — faster than many dog breeds can sustain over the same short distance.

components.note: 罒 (a net) — the law closing in around wrongdoing
非 (wrong) — the wrongdoing itself, caught in the net
心 (heart) — 恶 relates to an evil or malicious state of heart/mind
亚 (yà) gives a sound distantly related to 恶's reading è, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 他终于为自己的罪恶付出了代价。
example.pinyin: tā zhōngyú wèi zìjǐ de zuìè fùchū le dàijià.
example.english: He finally paid the price for his own wrongdoing.
example.fact: Dante's 'Inferno,' written in the early 14th century, organized sin into nine concentric circles of Hell ranked by severity — a literary structure so influential that it still shapes modern pop-culture depictions of moral hierarchy seven centuries later.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 活 relates to water flowing, a symbol of life and vitality.
舌 (shé) gives a hint of the sound — 活 is pronounced huó, a connection that has shifted over time.
儿 (simplified from 兒) depicts a small child, drawn with a large head on a small body — a simple picture of youth.

example.hanzi: 今天家里的活儿都干完了。
example.pinyin: jīntiān jiā lǐ de huór dōu gàn wán le.
example.english: Today all the housework at home has been finished.
example.fact: The 40-hour workweek wasn't standardized in the US until the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938; before that, many factory laborers, including children, routinely worked 60-plus hours a week under grueling industrial-era conditions.

components.note: 用's earliest forms pictured a wooden bucket or pail, an everyday household tool. From the concrete image of a useful container, the character broadened over time into the abstract verb 'to use.'
Originally depicted a wheat plant; this agricultural picture was borrowed early on to represent the unrelated verb 'to come.'

example.hanzi: 这个房间专门用来存放旧书。
example.pinyin: zhè ge fángjiān zhuānmén yònglái cúnfàng jiù shū.
example.english: This room is used specifically for storing old books.
example.fact: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault, carved into a mountainside in the Arctic, stores backup samples of over a million crop seed varieties from around the world at -18°C, in case natural disasters or war destroy the original crops.

components.note: 辶 (walking/movement) — relates to 远's meaning 'far, distant,' a long way to walk.
元 (yuán) gives a sound hint — 远 is pronounced yuǎn, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
辶 (walking/movement) — relates to 远's meaning 'far, distant,' a long way to walk.
元 (yuán) gives a sound hint — 远 is pronounced yuǎn, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 他的成绩远远超过了其他同学。
example.pinyin: tā de chéngjì yuǎnyuǎn chāoguò le qítā tóngxué.
example.english: His grades far exceeded those of his classmates.
example.fact: Voyager 1, launched in 1977, is now more than 24 billion kilometers from Earth — farther than any human-made object has ever traveled — and its radio signals still take over 22 hours to reach us.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 哈 is the sound made by the mouth while laughing
合 (hé) gives a sound related to 哈's reading hā, from an older, closer pronunciation link
禾 (grain, a growing rice or wheat plant) — 利 pictures a harvest.
刂 (knife) — cutting grain at harvest time was a clear benefit or gain, giving 利 its meaning 'profit' or 'advantage.'

example.hanzi: 电影里的哈利最终打败了敌人。
example.pinyin: diànyǐng lǐ de Hālì zuìzhōng dǎbài le dírén.
example.english: Harry in the movie eventually defeated the enemy.
example.fact: Harry Houdini performed his famous 'Chinese Water Torture Cell' escape thousands of times over a decade — submerged upside down in a locked, water-filled tank, he had roughly three minutes to escape before running out of air.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 扫 describes using the hand to sweep.
帚 depicts a hand-held broom — held by the hand 扌, it gave 扫 its meaning 'to sweep.'
扌 (hand) — 描 describes tracing or drawing something by hand.
苗 (miáo) is an exact match for the sound of 描.

example.hanzi: 医生让他去做一次全身扫描。
example.pinyin: yīshēng ràng tā qù zuò yī cì quánshēn sǎomiáo.
example.english: The doctor had him get a full-body scan.
example.fact: The first CT scanner, built by Godfrey Hounsfield in 1971, took over five hours to scan a single brain and nearly two and a half hours to process the resulting image; modern scanners now do the equivalent in seconds.

components.note: 亻 (person) — represents a human figure.

叚 depicts borrowing or handing something over — a person who is not genuine, or something borrowed rather than real, gave 假 its meaning 'false, fake' (and, for a break from routine, 'vacation, leave.')
月 (moon) — 期 relates to time measured by the moon's cycles, like a period or term.
其 (qí) gives a hint of the sound — 期 is pronounced qī, a connection that has shifted slightly in tone.

example.hanzi: 暑假是学生们最喜欢的假期。
example.pinyin: shǔjià shì xuéshēngmen zuì xǐhuān de jiàqī.
example.english: Summer break is students' favorite vacation.
example.fact: France mandates by law that every full-time employee receive a minimum of five weeks of paid vacation annually, one of the most generous statutory minimums in the world, compared to the US, which has no federal law guaranteeing any paid vacation at all.

components.note: 缶 (a clay jar) — 缺 relates to something broken or missing, like a cracked vessel.
夬 (guài) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading quē has diverged.
之 depicts a foot stepping forward.
丿 marks a barrier in front of the foot — a step blocked by a wall gave 乏 its meaning 'lacking, tired.'

example.hanzi: 这个地区长期缺乏干净的饮用水。
example.pinyin: zhè ge dìqū chángqí quēfá gānjìng de yǐnyòngshuǐ.
example.english: This region has long lacked clean drinking water.
example.fact: According to the WHO, roughly 2 billion people worldwide still lack access to safely managed drinking water at home, and unsafe water contributes to over 500,000 diarrheal deaths every year, disproportionately affecting children under five.

components.note: ⺷ (sheep, related to 羊) — 义 relates to what is right or moral, linked to the idea of sacrificial sheep used in rituals of righteousness.
乂 (yì) gives the sound — 义 is also pronounced yì, an exact match.
力 (strength, effort) anchors 务/務, showing exertion put toward a task.
攴 (a hand wielding a tool) appears in the traditional 務, picturing someone striving hard at labor — together the pieces built the idea of 'duty' or 'affairs' that must be attended to with effort.

example.hanzi: 纳税是每个公民的义务。
example.pinyin: nàshuì shì měi gè gōngmín de yìwù.
example.english: Paying taxes is every citizen's duty.
example.fact: Switzerland still practices a form of mandatory national service, requiring most male citizens to complete military duty and remain part of a reserve into their 30s, letting the country mobilize a large trained force despite having a small standing army.

components.note: 车 (cart) — the vehicle moving goods.
辶 (walking/movement) — the cart traveling along a road, linking one place to another, giving 连 its meaning 'to connect, link.'
纟 (thread) — 续 relates to continuing, like an unbroken thread
卖 (mài) gives a loose sound connection to 续's reading xù

example.hanzi: 这支球队已经连续赢了十场比赛。
example.pinyin: zhè zhī qiúduì yǐjīng liánxù yíng le shí chǎng bǐsài.
example.english: This team has won ten games in a row.
example.fact: The longest winning streak in major North American pro sports belongs to the 1971-72 Los Angeles Lakers, who won 33 consecutive NBA games — a record that has stood for over 50 years and is still considered one of the hardest in sports to break.

components.note: A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.
日 (sun/day) — relates to 时's meaning of 'time, season'; the phonetic part of the character was later replaced by 寸 in the simplified form

example.hanzi: 他一时想不起那个人的名字。
example.pinyin: tā yīshí xiǎng bù qǐ nà ge rén de míngzi.
example.english: He couldn't recall that person's name for a moment.
example.fact: Short-term memory typically holds only about four to seven items at once for a matter of seconds unless they're actively rehearsed — a limit famously described in psychologist George Miller's 1956 paper 'The Magical Number Seven.'

components.note: Originally depicted a burning candle or the sun's rays radiating outward — the source of 白's meaning 'white, bright, clear.'
大 (a person, arms outstretched) — represents a human being.
一 (a line, here representing the sky) — drawn above a person, showing what is above them: the heavens, hence 'sky, day.'

example.hanzi: 他白天工作,晚上上课。
example.pinyin: tā báitiān gōngzuò, wǎnshang shàngkè.
example.english: He works during the day and attends classes at night.
example.fact: North of the Arctic Circle, parts of Norway experience the Midnight Sun, where the sun doesn't set at all for up to 76 consecutive days each summer, turning 'daytime' into a continuous, round-the-clock event.

components.note: 欠 (to lack) — wanting something you lack ties to 欲's meaning 'desire.'
谷 (gǔ) gives a sound distantly related to yù, having drifted apart over time.
Depicts a person standing tall, gazing up at the moon 月 — the image of looking into the distance, the source of 望's meaning 'to gaze, hope, expect.'

example.hanzi: 金钱无法满足他所有的欲望。
example.pinyin: jīnqián wúfǎ mǎnzú tā suǒyǒu de yùwàng.
example.english: Money can't satisfy all of his desires.
example.fact: Dopamine, often called the 'desire molecule,' spikes in the brain not at the moment of reward but during the anticipation of it — a mechanism confirmed in 1990s primate studies that helps explain why craving something can feel more intense than actually getting it.

components.note: 鬼 (ghost) — 魔 names a demon or evil spirit.
麻 (má) gives a sound distantly related to mó, having drifted apart over time.

术 began as a pictograph of a millet plant with grains hanging from its stalk. In the traditional character 術 (skill, technique), this millet sign sat inside 行 (a crossroads radical) as a sound element; simplified Chinese later kept just the millet shape to stand for the whole idea of 'technique' or 'art.'

example.hanzi: 他在派对上表演了一个魔术。
example.pinyin: tā zài pàiduì shàng biǎoyǎn le yī gè móshù.
example.english: He performed a magic trick at the party.
example.fact: The largest magic trick ever performed was David Copperfield's 1983 'vanishing' of the Statue of Liberty, where he made the 151-foot statue seem to disappear in front of a live audience using a rotating platform and carefully timed lighting.

components.note: 车 (cart) — the vehicle moving goods.
辶 (walking/movement) — the cart traveling along a road, linking one place to another, giving 连 its meaning 'to connect, link.'
王 (a variant of 玉, jade) — 环 originally referred to a round jade ring or bracelet
不 (bù) gives a sound distantly related to 环's reading huán, having drifted apart considerably over time

example.hanzi: 这是一部连环画风格的漫画。
example.pinyin: zhè shì yī bù liánhuán huà fēnggé de mànhuà.
example.english: This is a comic drawn in a serial-panel picture-book style.
example.fact: The ancient Chinese mechanical puzzle known as the Nine Linked Rings dates back over 2,000 years and requires a minimum of 341 moves to fully separate all nine interlocking rings, making it one of the earliest known combinatorial puzzles in the world.

components.note: 虫 (insect) — honey is made by bees, which are insects.
宓 (mì) gives the sound — an exact match for 蜜.
虫 (insect) — a bee is a kind of insect.
夆 (féng in related characters) gives a sound close to fēng, sharing the same rhyme.

example.hanzi: 一群蜜蜂正在花丛中采蜜。
example.pinyin: yī qún mìfēng zhèngzài huācóng zhōng cǎimì.
example.english: A swarm of bees is gathering nectar among the flowers.
example.fact: A single honeybee colony can visit up to 2 million flowers to produce just one pound of honey, and worker bees communicate the direction and distance of food sources to each other through a precise 'waggle dance.'

meanings: (after a noun N and before a predicate P) the reason why N P

components.note: A stylized foot (related to 止, 'to stop/foot') — originally meant 'to go,' later grammaticalized into a literary possessive/linking particle, similar to 的.
户 (door) — 所 evokes a location or place, such as where a door stands.
斤 (axe) — combined with 户 (door), the image of an axe at a door gave rise to the abstract sense of 'a place' or 'that which.'

以's early form pictured a person bent over, carrying or lifting an object such as a farming tool. From the concrete act of 'taking up' something, the character broadened into the abstract sense of 'by means of, using, because of.'

example.hanzi: 他之所以迟到,是因为路上堵车。
example.pinyin: tā zhīsuǒyǐ chídào, shì yīnwèi lùshang dǔchē.
example.english: The reason he was late is that there was traffic on the road.
example.fact: The world's longest recorded traffic jam occurred in China in August 2010 on the Beijing-Tibet Expressway, stretching roughly 100 kilometers and trapping some drivers for more than 10 days as construction and truck congestion piled up.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — relates directly to 拉's meaning 'to pull, drag,' an action done by hand.
立 (lì) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted noticeably from lā.
其 (a winnowing basket) forms the left side of 斯, tied to the character's original meaning of splitting grain from chaff.

斤 (axe) on the right shows the tool used to cleave apart. Over time 斯's core meaning of 'to split' faded, and its sound was borrowed as a near-universal syllable for transliterating foreign words, as in 拉斯维加斯 (Las Vegas).
纟 (thread/silk) — 维 relates to a connecting thread or fiber, extended to mean 'to maintain, to link'
隹 (zhuī) gives a loose sound connection to 维's reading wéi
力 (strength) — 加 pictures adding one's effort to a cause.
口 (mouth, words) — combining strength with words of support gave 加 its meaning 'to add' or 'to increase.'
其 (a winnowing basket) forms the left side of 斯, tied to the character's original meaning of splitting grain from chaff.

斤 (axe) on the right shows the tool used to cleave apart. Over time 斯's core meaning of 'to split' faded, and its sound was borrowed as a near-universal syllable for transliterating foreign words, as in 拉斯维加斯 (Las Vegas).

example.hanzi: 很多游客专门飞去拉斯维加斯看演出。
example.pinyin: hěn duō yóukè zhuānmén fēi qù Lāsīwéijiāsī kàn yǎnchū.
example.english: Many tourists fly specifically to Las Vegas to see shows.
example.fact: Las Vegas sits in the middle of the Mojave Desert, yet the city has become a leader in water recycling, treating and returning nearly 99% of indoor water use back to Lake Mead despite its famous fountains and pools.

components.note: 宀 (roof, house) tops 实/實, setting the scene inside a home.

毌 pictures a string of valuables such as strung coins or shells; a house full of such wealth gave 实 its core sense of being 'substantial, full, real' — the same idea behind 实力, tangible strength you can actually draw on.
力 depicts the blade of a plow — since plowing fields took great physical effort, the shape came to represent strength or power.

example.hanzi: 这支球队的实力不容小觑。
example.pinyin: zhè zhī qiúduì de shílì bù róng xiǎoqiào.
example.english: This team's strength should not be underestimated.
example.fact: The US Navy's Nimitz-class aircraft carriers each displace over 100,000 tons and carry roughly 90 aircraft, giving a single ship more raw military strength than the entire air force of most countries in the world.

components.note: 米 (grain, especially husked rice) — 精's meaning 'refined, essence, spirit' relates to rice refined to its purest form.
青 (qīng) gives a sound hint — 精 is pronounced jīng, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant differs.
火 (fire) — linked to ritual fires once used to try to communicate with spirits
彐 (jì) gives a sound distantly related to 灵's reading líng, having drifted apart considerably over time

example.hanzi: 这部动画里有一个调皮的小精灵。
example.pinyin: zhè bù dònghuà lǐ yǒu yī gè tiáopí de xiǎo jīnglíng.
example.english: There's a mischievous little sprite in this animated show.
example.fact: Iceland's national road agency has, on occasion, rerouted actual highway construction around large boulders because of public belief in 'hidden folk,' elf-like spirits said to live inside rocks — a modern accommodation rooted in centuries-old Icelandic folklore.

components.note: 大 (great, big) — boasting or praising both involve making something out to be great.
亏 (kuī) gives a sound close to kuā, sharing the initial consonant.
弓 (bow) — relates to 张's original meaning 'to draw a bow taut,' extended to 'to open, stretch.'
长 (cháng) gives a sound hint — 张 is pronounced zhāng, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant and tone differ.

example.hanzi: 他说话总是有点夸张。
example.pinyin: tā shuōhuà zǒng shì yǒudiǎn kuāzhāng.
example.english: He always exaggerates a bit when he talks.
example.fact: American folktales about Paul Bunyan, a giant lumberjack supposedly responsible for carving the Grand Canyon by dragging his axe, are a well-documented example of the 19th-century 'tall tale' tradition, built entirely on outlandish exaggeration for entertainment.

components.note: 丿 (something falling) — an object slipping away.
夫 (a hand/person) — the object slipping out of a hand, giving 失 its meaning 'to lose.'
扌 (hand) — 控 relates to controlling or restraining something by hand
空 (kōng) gives the sound — an exact match with 控's reading kòng

example.hanzi: 汽车在冰面上突然失控打滑。
example.pinyin: qìchē zài bīngmiàn shàng tūrán shīkòng dǎhuá.
example.english: The car suddenly went out of control and skidded on the ice.
example.fact: The Chernobyl nuclear disaster of 1986 began when a routine safety test went out of control during a power surge, causing reactor 4 to explode; the resulting radioactive fallout was detected across most of Europe within days.

components.note: 木 (wood) marks 桌 as a piece of wooden furniture.
卓 (zhuó) supplied a sound close to zhuō and also carries a sense of 'standing tall,' fitting for a piece of furniture that stands up off the floor.
A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.

example.hanzi: 钥匙就放在桌上,你没看到吗?
example.pinyin: yàoshi jiù fàng zài zhuōshàng, nǐ méi kàndào ma?
example.english: The keys are right there on the table — didn't you see them?
example.fact: Formal dining etiquette around the table varies widely — in the UK, placing elbows on the table is traditionally considered rude, while in France it's commonly accepted and even expected during conversation between courses.

components.note: A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.
千 grew from the character 人 (person) with an added mark across the leg. Marking a person this way was a simple tally device that was borrowed to write the numeral 'thousand.'

example.hanzi: 这幅画拍卖出了一千多美元。
example.pinyin: zhè fú huà pāimài chū le yīqiān duō měiyuán.
example.english: This painting sold at auction for more than a thousand dollars.
example.fact: The Japanese tradition of folding 1,000 paper cranes, senbazuru, is believed to grant a wish and was popularized worldwide after Sadako Sasaki, a survivor of the Hiroshima bombing, attempted to fold 1,000 cranes before her death from leukemia in 1955.

components.note: 贝 (money) — gambling involves staking money.
者 (zhě) gives a sound distantly related to dǔ, having drifted apart over time.
十 (ten) — 博 relates to breadth, with ten symbolizing completeness.
尃 (fū) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading bó has diverged considerably.

example.hanzi: 长期赌博让他欠下了巨额债务。
example.pinyin: chángqí dǔbó ràng tā qiàn xià le jù'é zhàiwù.
example.english: Long-term gambling left him deeply in debt.
example.fact: The oldest known dice, carved from bone, date back roughly 5,000 years to sites in Iran, showing that games of chance and gambling-like behavior are among the oldest recorded human pastimes, predating written history in many cultures.

components.note: 夂 (a foot, to go) — 处 relates to arriving somewhere.
卜 (a mark or flag) — planting a marker after arriving gave 处 its meaning of 'a place' or 'to settle, deal with.'
土 (earth) — 境 relates to land and territory, extended to mean 'environment, boundary'
竟 (jìng) gives the sound — 境 is also pronounced jìng, an exact match

example.hanzi: 公司目前的处境十分艰难。
example.pinyin: gōngsī mùqián de chǔjìng shífēn jiānnán.
example.english: The company's current situation is very difficult.
example.fact: Ernest Shackleton's 1915 Antarctic expedition became one of history's most famous survival situations when their ship Endurance was crushed by pack ice; all 28 crew members nonetheless survived over a year stranded on ice and in open boats before a daring rescue.
